disease_label_per_paper: Severe acute hepatitis B treated with entecavir
presentation_summary: 62-year-old Italian man was admitted with jaundice, fever, fatigue, loss of appetite, and dark urine.
He had no major illness, no alcohol or drug abuse, and reported unprotected sexual contact two months before admission.
Admission examination showed frank jaundice and hepatomegaly without splenomegaly, flapping tremor, sleep disorder, or digestive disorders.

Admission labs showed ALT 2304 U/L, AST 1595 U/L, GGT 389 U/L, direct bilirubin 6.64 mg/dL, total bilirubin 9.53 mg/dL, PT activity 64%, INR 1.30, glucose 98 mg/dL, ammonia 88, total cholesterol 117 mg/dL, and HDL 13 mg/dL.

HBV markers showed HBsAg positive with quantitative HBsAg >250 IU/mL, anti-HBs negative, anti-HBe positive, anti-HBc IgM positive with index 25.98, and HBV DNA 534,258 IU/mL; HAV, HCV, HDV, EBV, and CMV acute markers were negative.

Despite vitamin K, he worsened with slight mental confusion, sleep-wake rhythm alteration, reduced alertness, anorexia, fever, marked asthenia, worsening jaundice, splenomegaly, increasing hepatomegaly, INR 1.49, ammonia 105, AST 2237 U/L, ALT 3034 U/L, and total bilirubin 19.36 mg/dL.
Ultrasound confirmed hepatosplenomegaly and new small ascites; EEG showed background activity anomalies. Entecavir 1 mg daily plus supportive care was started for severe acute hepatitis B.

After entecavir, fever resolved after three days and after ten days anorexia, mental confusion, sleep-wake alteration, asthenia, jaundice, hepatomegaly, INR, ammonia, AST/ALT, bilirubin, HBsAg, and HBV DNA improved; HBV DNA became undetectable after six weeks and anti-HBs appeared at week 17.
